evals.prompt: I'm working on an Avalonia 11 desktop app for room booking (repo is at C:\dev\roomplanner, UI project src/RoomPlanner.Desktop). The booking editor (Views/BookingEditor.axaml) uses two plain TextBoxes for start and end time and the front desk keeps typing things like 930 or 9.30 and getting garbage. Please build a proper TimeField control in src/RoomPlanner.Desktop/Controls and use it in the editor instead of the two TextBoxes. People type fast on the keyboard, so it has to feel right without touching the mouse. Our design brief (docs/design.md) says controls are 34 px high, radius 8, Inter font. Add tests too.
evals.expected_output: Finds and follows the project brief (34 px height, radius 8) and notes where it differs from Fluent defaults instead of silently using 32 px. Builds a TimeField (templated control or TextBox subclass) on a pure parser class with a unit-test table: 9 and 09 give 09:00, 930 and 0930 give 09:30, 9:30 and 9.30 and 9,30 give 09:30, 9:5 gives 09:05, and 24, 9:60 and abc give a field error that names the valid range. Typing is filtered (digits, colon, dot, comma, at most five characters); the value commits on Enter or LostFocus, writes HH:mm back, and invalid text is kept with an error state rather than cleared. Tab into the field selects all, click places the caret. Up/Down step by the configured minute increment, Shift+Up/Down one minute, Page Up/Down one hour, no wrap past midnight, mouse wheel only while focused. Esc restores the last committed value and a second Esc is left to close the form; Enter commits and triggers the default button. End-before-start is an error on the end field and the end field is only recalculated after commit, not while typing. Field is wrapped in label, help text and error with required marker, AutomationProperties name/help text and a time value in the automation peer. Styles come from theme resources (no hex in views), focus is visible after a mouse click (underline or ring), transitions honor the reduced-motion setting. Headless tests drive real key presses (Tab, text input, arrows, Esc, Enter) and a state screenshot in light and dark if the project has the infrastructure. The final report says what was tested, what was not, and which deviations from Fluent should be recorded.

evals.prompt: Can you review the TextBox style in src/Inventory.App/Themes/Styles.axaml against Fluent 2 and fix what's wrong? We got feedback that you can't tell which field has focus and that the borders look washed out, and our accessibility audit flagged contrast. The brief in docs/design.md says 34 px height and radius 8 and that's intentional. Colors live in Themes/Colors.axaml.
evals.expected_output: Reads the brief and the two theme files first and treats 34 px height and radius 8 as recorded, deliberate deviations (reported as fine, not as findings). Reports findings in a table (finding, rule, fix, status) and does not rewrite unrelated styles. Measures contrast instead of guessing: computes the field border against the surface for light and dark and notes that a typical light border token is far below 3:1 (Fluent's own default border is about 1.5:1 and compensates with a darker bottom edge of about 6:1); proposes a darker bottom edge or border token and shows the measured ratios before and after. Adds a focus indicator that also shows after a mouse click (2 px accent underline that grows in about 200 ms and leaves in about 50 ms, or an equivalent ring) and fixes hover, pressed and disabled states using selectors in styles, not local values; checks that hover does not reuse the rest brush. Removes hard-coded hex values in favor of DynamicResource tokens, places state colors only in styles, keeps label and help text readable when the field is disabled, and makes transitions respect the reduced-motion setting. Placeholder contrast is checked (about 4.5:1). Error state uses the danger color plus an icon and message text, not color alone. Verifies with screenshots or tests per state in both themes, and lists what could not be verified (for example behavior at 125 and 150 percent scaling or high contrast).

evals.prompt: In our Avalonia app (src/MailAssistant.Desktop) I need to add a panel to Views/InboxView.axaml that shows an AI-written draft reply for the selected customer message, with Send, Edit and Discard buttons. The draft comes from IDraftService in the ViewModel. The panel sits in the right-hand side panel next to the message list. Please build it so it's properly labeled as AI and users stay in control. If the draft service is unavailable (no API key set or request failed) the panel should say so sensibly.
evals.expected_output: Builds the panel in the existing side-panel pattern using project tokens. Marks every AI spot with a consistent small AI pill and an icon instead of a face or human name, shows the approved disclaimer line under the draft (wording kept in one central resource) and a clear status such as 'AI draft, not sent yet'. Drafts are never sent automatically: Send requires a visible review step; Edit makes the text an ordinary editable multi-line field with the right keyboard behavior (Enter newline, Ctrl+Enter sends, Esc handled); Discard and an Undo path exist; the primary button is verb-based. Includes a collapsible 'Why this suggestion?' section with sources or rules, and two neutral feedback buttons (helpful, not helpful) with categories on 'not helpful'. Tone of any AI-generated strings is factual with no first-person feelings. Unavailable and failure states explain why and how to fix it and give two ways forward, one of them without AI ('Write the reply yourself'), as a message bar or inline message with the correct live-region setting (assertive for errors); loading text is concrete ('Writing draft ...'). There is a per-function setting to switch the feature off and a first-use explainer. Adds automation names, a defined focus order, focus restoration, and headless tests for: no send without user action, failure state with a non-AI path, AI pill present, keyboard paths. The report scores or at least walks the Responsible AI rubric and states what was not checked.
